entries.answer: ART stands for Antiretroviral Therapy, and ARVs are the daily medicines used to treat HIV. They work by stopping the virus from multiplying in your body. This gives your immune system a chance to recover and keep you healthy.

While ART does not cure HIV, it keeps the virus under control by preventing it from making copies of itself. When the virus cannot multiply, your immune system stays strong. Taking your medicine every day is the key to keeping the virus weak.

question_patterns: why I must take drugs every day?
what if I stop taking my ARVs?
entries.answer: You must take your ARVs every day at the right time to keep a steady amount of medicine in your body. If you miss doses or stop taking them, the virus will start multiplying again and might become resistant to the drugs. Strict adherence is necessary to stay healthy.

question_patterns: what happen if I miss my dose?
I forgot to take my ARV today
entries.answer: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. But if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed one and just take the next one on schedule. Never take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Speak to your doctor if you miss doses often.

question_patterns: my drugs dey make me weak
do HIV drugs have side effects?
entries.answer: Some people might experience mild side effects like nausea, headaches, or vivid dreams when they first start ARVs. These usually go away after a few weeks as your body adjusts. If side effects are severe or don't stop, talk to your healthcare provider before stopping the drugs.

question_patterns: how I go know if my drugs dey work?
entries.answer: Viral load is the amount of HIV in your blood. When your ART is working well, your viral load will drop so low that standard tests can't even detect it. Getting to an 'undetectable' viral load is the main goal of taking HIV medication.

Your CD4 count measures the strength of your immune system by counting your CD4 cells, which fight infections. HIV attacks these cells. Taking your ARVs helps your CD4 count go up, meaning your body is stronger and better able to fight off sickness.

question_patterns: where I fit get ARV for Nigeria?
how much is ART in Nigeria?
entries.answer: HIV treatment, including ARVs and tests, is completely free in Nigeria at government hospitals and many designated health centers supported by PEPFAR, Global Fund, and FHI360. You don't have to pay for the life-saving medication.
